title: Morning Edition
dek: Argentina's economic and moral argument, an attack on Ukrainian rescuers, two rings around a dead star, and a library's seed exchange.

lead_story.headline: Pope Leo visits Argentina as tensions over austerity and Iran loom
lead_story.summary: Leo's first visit to Argentina follows his stop in Uruguay and comes amid disagreements between church leaders and President Javier Milei about poverty, government spending and the Iran war. Their public encounter has not yet occurred.
lead_story.why_it_matters: The visit puts a moral argument about economic adjustment alongside a government's case for reducing inflation and restoring fiscal stability.

items.headline: Russian drone strikes rescuers at site of deadly Ukrainian shelter attack
items.summary: Ukraine's emergency service says a Russian drone damaged rescue equipment at Komyshuvakha while crews worked at a former school and aid shelter struck earlier in the week. No rescuers were reported injured in the latest strike; Ukraine says the earlier attack killed at least 55.
items.why_it_matters: Repeated attacks at a disaster scene complicate search and identification work; casualty figures and attribution are based on Ukrainian authorities' reporting.

items.headline: Iran-war uncertainty rattles Gulf markets
items.summary: Saudi and Qatari stock indexes fell Sunday as traders weighed renewed reports of attacks around Iran, the U.S. blockade and possible escalation. Some claims about mine strikes and explosions remain unverified or contested.
items.why_it_matters: The regional financial response reflects fears that a conflict around vital shipping routes could intensify and affect energy supplies.

items.headline: Astronomers find two rings of planetary debris around a dead star
items.summary: Observations of white dwarf J1328−1450 reveal distinct rings of rocky debris with different magnesium signatures. Researchers propose disrupted planetary bodies as a possible explanation, but the history of the material remains uncertain.
items.why_it_matters: The system provides a rare observational window into the aftermath of planetary systems as their stars age.

items.headline: Greenland's parliament backs a security deal with Denmark and the United States
items.summary: Greenlandic lawmakers approved an agreement allowing expanded defense cooperation while retaining Greenland's self-government and Danish ties. Danish parliamentary consideration remains necessary.
items.why_it_matters: The debate is about security and Greenlanders' political agency, not merely the strategic preferences of larger countries.

items.headline: Older catch-up: new Martian gas observations raise possibility of ongoing volcanism
items.summary: Scientists reported hydrogen chloride over fissures near Alba Mons and suggested it might reflect underground magmatic activity. The proposed mechanism is an interpretation, not a confirmed observation of erupting magma.
items.why_it_matters: The finding could revise assumptions about Mars's internal activity and the environments where subsurface water might persist.

items.headline: Guelph library hosts a native-plant seed exchange
items.summary: Guelph Public Library and the local seed library scheduled a free November 7 gathering for seed sharing, composting advice and native-plant gardening. The report describes the planned event; attendance and outcomes were not independently confirmed.
items.why_it_matters: It is an ordinary example of local knowledge and resources being shared in a public institution.

items.headline: What if doing the right thing means choosing among several good things?
items.summary: Philosopher Irene McMullin argues that moral conflict often comes from competing legitimate demands on limited time and attention, not a simple battle between duty and selfish desire. She proposes evaluating choices in the context of a whole life.
items.why_it_matters: The essay offers a framework for moral tradeoffs when family, work, community and personal projects all make reasonable claims.

worth_your_time.headline: Argentina's proposed AI boom confronts Patagonia's resource limits
worth_your_time.summary: AP reports on President Milei's plans to attract data centers with regulatory and tax incentives, while residents question energy, water and employment promises. Some proposed investments remain at early stages.
worth_your_time.why_it_matters: The story connects technology investment to land use, energy planning, local consent and whether projected economic benefits will materialize.

reflection.passage: Till this moment, I never knew myself.
reflection.author: Jane Austen
reflection.context: Elizabeth Bennet realizes that pride in her own discernment has made her misread both Darcy and Wickham. The insight is painful because it forces her to revise her picture of herself.
reflection.question: Which convictions about yourself would be hardest to revise?
